review_notes: I read all 652 lines of LeanPool/LeanModularForms/GeneralizedResidueTheory/Residue/SectorCurve.lean, then checked the imported definition file GeneralizedResidueTheory/Basic.lean (cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand', cauchyPrincipalValue', CauchyPrincipalValueExists' and their @[simp] lemmas) and the downstream consumer Residue/SectorCurveLemma.lean. I also grepped the whole pool for uses of cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'_of_gt/_of_le (no uses anywhere), pv_integrand_seg* and the sectorCurve_* evaluation/norm lemmas. The findings concern (1) the integrand being written as an expanded if instead of the library's cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand' (so the existing @[simp] interface is dead in this file), (2) the per-segment integrand lemmas not being stated in the form their consumers need and being bypassed inside this very file, and (3) the segment rewrite lemmas overlapping at t = 1 and t = 2 with only propositionally equal right-hand sides. I did not run Lean, so I do not claim any of the proposed statements compile; they are given as concrete shapes consistent with the definitions and the existing lemmas.

findings.declaration: pv_cutoff_F_integrable_0_delta (same pattern in all private pv_cutoff_* lemmas, lines 307-574, and in pv_sector_cutoff_eq)
findings.excerpt:
let F : ℝ → ℂ := fun t => if ‖sectorCurve r α t - 0‖ > ε
        then (sectorCurve r α t)⁻¹ * deriv (sectorCurve r α) t else 0
    IntervalIntegrable F volume 0 (ε / r) := by
  set F : ℝ → ℂ := fun t => if ‖sectorCurve r α t - 0‖ > ε
      then (sectorCurve r α t)⁻¹ * deriv (sectorCurve r α) t else 0
findings.problem: Every statement of the cutoff development re-spells the integrand as an expanded `if ‖sectorCurve r α t - 0‖ > ε then (sectorCurve r α t)⁻¹ * deriv (sectorCurve r α) t else 0`, both in a `let F` in the type and again in a `set F` in the proof. That expression is definitionally `cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand' (fun z => z⁻¹) (sectorCurve r α) 0 ε t` (Basic.lean:64-66), but because the abbreviation is expanded, the library's canonical simp rules for it are unusable, and each proof must redo `dsimp only [F]; simp only [sub_zero]; rw [ite_eq_left]` / `rw [ite_eq_right (not_lt.mpr _)]` (e.g. lines 319, 505, 528, 559, 597, 606). Consequently `cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'_of_gt` and `_of_le` have no uses anywhere in the repository.
findings.proposed_change: Introduce one abbreviation, e.g. `abbrev sectorPVIntegrand (r α ε : ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℂ := cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand' (fun z => z⁻¹) (sectorCurve r α) 0 ε t` (or simply write `cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand' (fun z => z⁻¹) (sectorCurve r α) 0 ε` directly), use it in place of the `let F` in every private lemma and in `pv_sector_cutoff_eq` (lines 578-583), and replace each `rw [ite_eq_left h]` / `rw [ite_eq_right h]` with `rw [cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'_of_gt (by ...)]` / `rw [cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'_of_le (by ...)]`; then drop the `set F` lines.
findings.benefit: The statements one definition away from what `CauchyPrincipalValueExists'`/`cauchyPrincipalValue'` unfold to become literally the canonical form used downstream (SectorCurveLemma.lean uses `cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand' (fun z => z⁻¹) (sectorCurve r α) 0 ε` throughout), the existing `@[simp]` interface in Basic.lean becomes effective instead of dead, and eight copies of the same two-line `let`/`set` boilerplate disappear. No mathematics changes, since the two forms are definitionally equal.

findings.excerpt:
/-- The integrand on segment 2 (t in (1,2)) simplifies to `I * alpha`. -/
theorem pv_integrand_seg2 (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (α : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Ioo 1 2) :
    (sectorCurve r α t)⁻¹ * deriv (sectorCurve r α) t = I * ↑α := by
  rw [sectorCurve_seg2 r α t ⟨le_of_lt ht.1, le_of_lt ht.2⟩,
      deriv_sectorCurve_seg2 r α t ht]
findings.problem: These three lemmas describe the *inner* product only, with no statement about the cutoff. Every real use is inside the piecewise integrand: the downstream consumer must write `simp only [cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand', sub_zero]; rw [ite_eq_left]; exact pv_integrand_seg2 ...` (SectorCurveLemma.lean:388-389, similarly 364-365), and this file's own `pv_cutoff_integral_seg2_eq_Ialpha` (lines 526-536) does not use `pv_integrand_seg2` at all but repeats `rw [sectorCurve_seg2 ..., deriv_sectorCurve_seg2 ...]; field_simp`. So the published simplification lemma does not serve the simplification step it is named for, and that step is duplicated three times in this file and twice more downstream.
findings.proposed_change: Add companion lemmas whose left-hand side is the canonical integrand, e.g. `theorem cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'_inv_of_seg2 (h : t ∈ Ioo 1 2) (hε : ε < ‖sectorCurve r α t‖) : cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand' (fun z => z⁻¹) (sectorCurve r α) 0 ε t = I * ↑α` proved by `rw [cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'_of_gt hε]; exact pv_integrand_seg2 r hr α t h`, with the analogous seg1/seg3 statements; tag these `@[simp]` (the arc one in particular, whose right-hand side `I * ↑α` does not mention `t`, so there is no rewrite cycle). Then the `h_on_Ioo` blocks at lines 504-513, 526-536, 557-570 can each be discharged by the companion lemma instead of `dsimp only [F]; ...; field_simp`.
findings.benefit: The per-segment simplification becomes a single rewrite usable in exactly the context where it is needed (inside `cauchyPrincipalValueIntegrand'`), removing three duplicated `field_simp` blocks here and the unfold-then-rewrite dance downstream.

findings.excerpt:
theorem sectorCurve_seg2 (r : ℝ) (α : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc 1 2) :
    sectorCurve r α t = ↑r * exp (I * ↑((t - 1) * α)) := by
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le ht.1 with rfl | h1
  · simp [sectorCurve, Complex.exp_zero]
  · simp only [sectorCurve, ite_eq_right (not_le.mpr h1), ite_eq_left ht.2]
findings.problem: The segment lemmas are the only rewrite rules this file offers for `sectorCurve r α t`, and they are the rules every proof in this file and in SectorCurveLemma.lean uses (`rw [sectorCurve_seg1 ...]`, `rw [sectorCurve_seg3 ...]`). Their domains are not the definition's branches: `sectorCurve` guards are `t ≤ 1`, `t ≤ 2`, else (lines 64-70), so on `t = 1` the first branch wins and on `t = 2` the second branch wins, yet `sectorCurve_seg2` claims the arc form on all of `Icc 1 2` and `sectorCurve_seg3` claims the ray form on all of `Icc 2 3`. At those shared endpoints the right-hand sides are only propositionally equal to the neighbouring rule's (`↑r * exp (I * ↑((1 - 1) * α))` versus `↑(1 * r)`), which is why the proofs above need `rcases eq_or_lt_of_le ht.1` plus `Complex.exp_zero` (line 107) and `push_cast; ring_nf` (lines 114-116); `sectorCurve_seg1` needs no such split. Any attempt to register these as simp rules therefore produces competing rules on the overlap.
findings.proposed_change: State the segment lemmas on the definition's own, disjoint guards: `sectorCurve_seg1` on `Icc 0 1`, `sectorCurve_seg2` on `Ioc 1 2`, `sectorCurve_seg3` on `Ioc 2 3`, each proved by a single `simp only [sectorCurve, ite_eq_right ..., ite_eq_left ...]`. Keep the currently stated `Icc` versions (needed by the interval proofs) as corollaries derived via `sectorCurve_one` (line 90) and `sectorCurve_two` (line 94) for the left endpoints, so that each `t` matches exactly one segment rule.
findings.benefit: The segment rules become non-overlapping and confluent, so they can safely serve as the rewrite/simp interface for `sectorCurve`; the boundary case splits and `exp_zero`/`ring_nf` steps in `sectorCurve_seg2`/`sectorCurve_seg3` disappear, and users no longer have to remember that the `Icc` statements are only true up to the boundary identities.

def sectorCurve (r : ℝ) (α : ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  if t ≤ 1 then
    ↑(t * r)
  else if t ≤ 2 then
    ↑r * exp (I * ↑((t - 1) * α))
